screens.title: 1. Dashboard / GIS Map
screens.subtitle: Real-Time Network State, Disruption Telemetry & Leaflet Asset Map
screens.description: Consolidated operational nerve-center providing real-time situational awareness across the Delhi-Howrah mainline, integrating KPI summaries, emergency queues, corridor availability, and interactive GIS geospatial mapping.

explanation.A_what_is_this: The Dashboard / GIS Map is the executive operational landing page of ABPS v4.0. It integrates real-time network health, scheduled CP-SAT block status, pending asset maintenance alerts, and an interactive GIS spatial map across all 6 high-density corridor sections of Delhi Division.
explanation.B_why_included: Without a unified command dashboard, railway traffic controllers must cross-reference isolated logbooks, scada alarms, and train control charts. This section brings all operational threads into a single glass pane, allowing instant decision-making and rapid bottleneck identification.
C_features_available: 4-Card Critical KPI Ribbon summarizing active maintenance tasks, safety overrides, CP-SAT blocks, and conflict counts.
Maintenance Priority Queue with urgent work orders sorted by expected-loss ranking.
Interactive Leaflet GIS Map displaying track sections, active block possessions, and asset geolocations with popup inspectors.
Real-Time Corridor Availability Gauges and sectional traffic density meters.
Quick action triggers for emergency re-optimization and system-wide status refresh.
explanation.D_how_it_works: On initial render, CommandCenterView triggers concurrent asynchronous calls to /api/metrics, /api/tasks, and /api/network/corridors. As telemetry feeds in, priority scores are normalized, Leaflet polylines render corridor track segments colored by health status, and live WebSocket heartbeats keep counters synchronized.
explanation.E_user_interaction: Controllers scan top KPIs to detect anomalies, toggle between Weekly and Monthly horizons, click on urgent maintenance rows in the queue to inspect asset wear, and pan/zoom the GIS map to inspect specific track sections and OHE feeder stations.
explanation.F_output: Real-time visual map of corridor possessions, aggregated divisional maintenance metrics, and instant navigational entry points into deep diagnostic views.
explanation.G_cross_connections: Directly links to Section 2 (Asset Backlog) via priority queue rows, Section 3 (Weekly Block Planner) via block status chips, and Section 18 (Verification Suite) via the safety gate status badge.
explanation.H_practical_example: At 06:30 AM during morning peak, a Sectional Controller notices the 'Critical Tasks' badge turns red (15 urgent defects). By clicking the top urgent TRD task on the GIS map, the controller instantly sees a sagging catenary wire at KM 142/8 and initiates an emergency block recommendation before freight congestion peaks.
explanation.I_viva_defense_pitch: The Dashboard is our operational nerve-center. It combines mathematical telemetry with Leaflet GIS spatial mapping so divisional controllers can monitor 1,447 km of high-density track, 72 certified maintenance blocks, and 1,819 train movements in a single, conflict-free interface.
explanation.J_technical_architecture: Built with React 18, Tailwind CSS, Lucide icons, and React-Leaflet. Consumes Go Fiber REST endpoints (/api/metrics, /api/network/corridors) and communicates with the Python CP-SAT solver backend via asynchronous HTTP state hooks.

screens.title: 2. Asset Backlog
screens.subtitle: Unified Multi-Department Work Order Repository & Urgency Ranking
screens.description: Comprehensive maintenance task repository integrating work orders from Engineering (ENG), Traction Distribution (TRD), and Signal & Telecommunication (S&T) with expected-loss prioritization.

explanation.A_what_is_this: Asset Backlog is the centralized inventory of all pending, approved, and completed railway maintenance tasks across permanent way, overhead electrification, and signaling assets.
explanation.B_why_included: Historically, each railway department operated in silos using separate paper ledgers or disparate legacy databases. Asset Backlog unifies all departments into a standardized schema with rigorous priority scoring.
C_features_available: Unified task table showing Task ID, Department, Section, Duration, Criticality Score, and Deadline.
Department filter buttons (All, TRD, ENG, S&T, MECH) with dynamic counter badges.
Search input with instant filtering by asset ID, track kilometer, or supervisor name.
Priority distribution summary cards breaking down tasks by Critical, High, Medium, and Routine.
Direct action triggers to inspect asset health curves and manually adjust scheduling windows.
explanation.D_how_it_works: Tasks ingested from UIMS and manual work orders are evaluated by the Python urgency engine. Criticality is computed as a product of asset failure probability, line importance factor, and traffic gross million tonnes (GMT). Tasks exceeding threshold 90.0 trigger statutory safety overrides.
explanation.E_user_interaction: Supervisors filter tasks by their specific department, sort by impending statutory deadlines, search for specific track kilometers, and click tasks to view required machinery and crew logistics.
explanation.F_output: Standardized, urgency-ranked work order ledger ready for batch injection into the CP-SAT optimization engine.
explanation.G_cross_connections: Feeds directly into Section 3 (Weekly Block Planner) for timeline scheduling, Section 6 (Coordination Centre) for shadow bundling, and Section 11 (Asset Health) for USFD history.
explanation.H_practical_example: A Permanent Way Inspector logs an ultrasonic flaw detected at KM 142/8. The task enters Asset Backlog, is flagged as ENG with Criticality 96.7, and is immediately color-coded in red with a statutory 48-hour completion deadline.
explanation.I_viva_defense_pitch: Asset Backlog breaks departmental silos by aggregating engineering, traction, and signaling work orders into one place. Every task is scored with our expected-loss formula so life-safety track repairs always take precedence.
explanation.J_technical_architecture: Implemented in frontend/src/components/TasksView.tsx. Consumes /api/tasks REST endpoint with client-side fuzzy search and server-side pagination. Backed by PostgreSQL task tables and SQLite WAL mirror.

screens.title: 3. Task Generator
screens.subtitle: Cross-Departmental Maintenance Requirement Submission & Constraint-Certified Block Allocation
screens.description: Interactive cross-departmental maintenance intake and instant CP-SAT corridor feasibility evaluation engine. Enables Civil, Electrical (TRD), and S&T engineers to define work packages, select assets, configure 8-stage isolation/safety procedures, and immediately obtain constraint-certified block windows.

explanation.A_what_is_this: The Task Generator is the primary operational portal for field engineers across Indian Railways departments (Engineering/P-Way, Traction/TRD, and Signal & Telecom/S&T) to submit new maintenance requirements and generate conflict-free possession blocks.
explanation.B_why_included: Historically, maintenance requisitions were filed on fragmented paper slips or isolated division portals without spatial or timetable validation. The Task Generator unifies requirements intake, enforces safety isolation protocols, and executes immediate mathematical pre-validation against timetabled passenger trains.
C_features_available: Cross-Department Category Selector (Engineering, Traction, S&T) with department-tailored templates.
Geospatial Asset Selector linking directly to track centerline chainage, section codes, and GIS coordinates.
Comprehensive Maintenance Task Definition with preset engineering packages (Rail Replacement, Tamping, OHE Inspection, Point Machine Testing).
8-Stage Safety & Isolation Package Stepper (Site Preparation, Traffic Protection, 25kV OHE Isolation, Work Execution, Testing, Inspection, Restoration, Handover).
Instant CP-SAT Feasibility Assessment Engine testing candidate possession windows against timetabled trains.
explanation.D_how_it_works: The user selects a department, chooses a physical track asset from canonical inventory, selects a work package template, and specifies isolation requirements. Upon clicking Generate Task, the frontend calls POST /api/tasks/generate. The backend calculates Weibull failure urgency, searches the timetable graph for minimum 10-minute headway windows, and returns certified block options.
explanation.E_user_interaction_flow:
1. Department Selection: Click Civil Engineering, TRD, or S&T card.
2. Asset Selection: Choose asset from searchable dropdown or click on the embedded Leaflet track map.
3. Task Parameters: Select template (e.g. Rail Replacement), target date, and requested duration (minutes).
4. Safety & Isolation: Check required isolations (25kV Traction Power, Signalling Lockout) and select crew resources.
5. Dispatch: Click 'Generate Maintenance Task & Block Allocation'. Review certified block options and commit to the master schedule.
explanation.F_system_response_outputs: Generates a canonical task record (TASK-DH-xxxxxx), assigns an expected-loss priority score, returns certified block windows with zero train overlap, and displays a radar chart of section disruption impact.

G_information_handled.displays: Asset attributes (type, section, age, condition score), candidate block slots, timetable train traffic density, isolation checklists.
G_information_handled.collects: Department code, asset ID, task type, work description, target date, duration in minutes, urgency flag, isolation flags, allocated machine/crew resources.
G_information_handled.processes: Logistic urgency transformation, CP-SAT time-window feasibility validation, 10-minute statutory headway clearance calculation.
G_information_handled.returns: Task ID, certified candidate block timeslots, conflict radar telemetry, schedule commitment confirmation.

explanation.H_connections_to_other_sections: Tasks created here immediately populate Section 02 (Asset Backlog), Section 04 (Weekly Block Planner), Section 06 (Coordination Centre) for shadow-block pairing, and Section 15 (Human Review & Audit).
explanation.I_practical_example: A P-Way Section Engineer identifies track gauge widening near km 142 on Section SEC-DH-01. They open Task Generator, select Engineering -> Rail Replacement on Asset AST-DH-003582, set 180 min duration, require 25kV OHE isolation, and click Generate. The system finds a 02:15-05:15 nighttime window between freight trains with zero passenger delay.
explanation.J_presentation_speaking_notes: The Task Generator solves the root cause of railway coordination failure: fragmented work orders. By integrating department-specific safety templates with live timetable intelligence, field engineers receive mathematically certified possession windows in under 2 seconds instead of days of manual correspondence.
explanation.K_technical_implementation: Implemented in frontend/src/components/TaskGeneratorView.tsx using React state hooks for multi-step form wizard, React-Leaflet for asset coordinate pin drops, and Axios communicating with POST /api/tasks/generate. Validates required crew skills, machine availability, and 25kV traction power interlock rules before API dispatch.

screens.title: 4. Weekly Block Planner
screens.subtitle: CP-SAT 7-Day Corridor Block Schedule & Interactive Gantt Timeline
screens.description: Interactive Gantt timeline displaying Google OR-Tools CP-SAT optimized 7-day maintenance block allocations across all 6 corridor sections, guaranteed to be conflict-free against 1,819 timetable trains.

explanation.A_what_is_this: The Weekly Block Planner is the tactical scheduling canvas of ABPS v4.0. It renders a 7-day, 24-hour visual Gantt timeline of certified maintenance blocks allocated across Delhi Division's 6 corridor sections.
explanation.B_why_included: Manual scheduling of line blocks across saturated double-track lines frequently leads to canceled blocks, emergency train stoppages, or unsafe overlapping possessions. The Weekly Block Planner delivers mathematically certified, conflict-free block windows.
C_features_available: 6 Corridor Section Swimlanes (NDLS-GZB, GZB-ALJN, ALJN-TDL, TDL-ETW, ETW-CNB, CNB-PRYJ).
Interactive time grid spanning 00:00 to 24:00 across 7 calendar days with 1-hour graduation lines.
Color-coded block bars indicating department (TRD=Blue, ENG=Green, S&T=Amber, Integrated=Purple).
CP-SAT Optimization Trigger Button with live solving telemetry and singleflight mutex lock status.
Assigned Corridor Possessions Table listing approved start/end times, durations, and allocated track lines.
explanation.D_how_it_works: The backend Python optimizer runs Google OR-Tools CP-SAT. It models block allocations as non-overlapping interval variables subject to no-overlap constraints with train paths, statutory 10-minute headway buffers, machine availability, and daylight restrictions. The solved schedule is rendered via HTML5 canvas/SVG.
explanation.E_user_interaction: Controllers navigate calendar days using date selectors, hover over block bars to inspect allocated tasks and headway buffers, click blocks to open conflict inspectors, and click 'Run CP-SAT Optimizer' to re-solve after schedule disruptions.
explanation.F_output: Certified 7-day corridor possession roster ready for divisional sign-off and live TMS dispatch.
explanation.G_cross_connections: Directly linked to Section 6 (Coordination Centre) for shadow blocks, Section 8 (Train Conflicts) for headway auditing, and Section 17 (Human Review & Audit) for formal L4 sign-off.
explanation.H_practical_example: During weekend planning, the optimizer detects a 180-minute maintenance window between Kanpur and Prayagraj at 02:30 AM. It allocates a combined OHE wire replacement and track tamping possession, automatically keeping the UP line clear for Prayagraj Express.
explanation.I_viva_defense_pitch: The Weekly Block Planner is powered by Google OR-Tools CP-SAT. It converts complex railway constraints into mathematical equations, delivering 72 certified, conflict-free maintenance windows across 7 days with zero headway violations.
explanation.J_technical_architecture: Built with React 18 in frontend/src/components/GanttTab.tsx. Uses virtualized scrolling for smooth 60fps rendering across 168 hours of timeline data. Backed by engine/optimizer.py and Go Fiber orchestration proxy.
